#5107. Analyst: XRP Below $1 Revives a 70% Bounce Bet

Home » Trendsetter News » Analyst: XRP Below $1 Revives a 70% Bounce Bet

XRP’s dip below $1 has revived hopes of a roughly 70% rebound, with one analyst citing a similar August rally.

XRP could repeat a roughly 70% rebound from below $1, according to a crypto commentator who points to an August rally as the template. In a new YouTube episode, Zach Rector argues that another sharp recovery is possible, though the case rests largely on a historical chart comparison rather than a confirmed catalyst.

The chart discussion puts XRP’s latest low near $0.89. The analyst says an earlier slide to $0.98 in August was followed by a rise toward $1.70 within four or five days.

“I’m not here to guarantee that that’s coming again,” Zach Rector says, before overlaying the earlier price pattern onto the latest decline. The analyst also suggests XRP could revisit $2 quickly, without committing to a date.

The explanation centers on leverage: the host argues that downside liquidations have largely cleared, leaving market makers an incentive to drive prices higher. The transcript provides no liquidation figures, order-book data or positioning metrics to substantiate that view.

That distinction matters. A previous bounce illustrates how sharply XRP can recover, but it does not establish that selling pressure is exhausted or rule out another decline.

The more consequential adoption discussion concerns the analyst’s claim that 1,700 institutions, corporations and enterprises use Ripple solutions. Rector explicitly acknowledges that there is no breakdown showing how many use products involving XRP.

Zach Rector also defends Ripple’s emphasis on its RLUSD stablecoin, arguing that greater stablecoin liquidity could attract activity to the XRP Ledger.

A statement attributed to Old Glory Bank supports offering both XRP and stablecoins, with regulated stablecoins potentially better suited to payments where businesses require certainty of value.

Still, stablecoin issuance on the ledger should not be confused with evidence that every payment requires XRP as an intermediary. The YouTube video does not establish that connection, despite the host’s bullish interpretation.

Zach Rector also identifies a proposed lending protocol as a potential source of collateral demand.

For crypto enthusiasts, these are separate propositions to track: a short-term rebound based on chart resemblance, and a longer-term investment case that depends on measurable network activity, liquidity and actual XRP usage.

XRP has finally printed a local reversal: the price is forming one higher high after another. There's a good chance this quick recovery turns into something more significant sooner than we anticipate. XRP is trading at $0.9927, up around 11% from the $0.89 low of the drop. The price is back at the $0.99 area, which was the August low.

Hopefully, bulls pick up the rally, though for now the momentum is slow. The descending volume on the price upside suggests fading. The divergence of moving averages is an anti-volatility signal right now rather than anything else. All of them still sit above the price, with the nearest one around $1.13.

DeFi Development Corp. has reported another increase in its Solana treasury, adding 9,482 SOL and SOL equivalents to reach approximately 2.62 million. The November 16 SEC-filed statement describes ten consecutive weeks of holdings growth and a separate streak of 31 business days of dividends on its CHAD preferred stock. The pairing illustrates how companies built around crypto treasuries increasingly operate two different propositions: directional token exposure for common shareholders and an income-oriented capital instrument with its own terms.

The filing lists approximately 2,619,311 SOL and equivalents, up from 2,609,829 in its previous update. Management says the accumulation streak began in September following a return to active buying in late August. Its activities include acquisitions, staking, validator operations and other on-chain opportunities. That mix matters because not all increases in token inventory necessarily correspond to purchasing the same number of SOL on a spot exchange. A complete shareholder analysis should separate bought tokens from rewards, then compare the increase with changes in the company’s shares and outstanding claims.

The company says increasing SOL per share is a strategic objective. A coin count divided by a share count can illustrate one dimension of exposure, but it does not replace net asset value, cash-flow analysis or a review of dilution. Capital raised to buy SOL may increase total tokens while changing ownership percentages. Some holdings may also be subject to staking arrangements or operational constraints. Investors should examine the definitions attached to any company-specific per-share indicator before concluding that a higher treasury automatically improves common-equity returns.

For related context, see our earlier report on Solana corporate treasury results.

The firm’s variable-rate Series C perpetual preferred stock, CHAD, carries a reported 14% annual dividend rate as of the update. The company says it has made payments for 31 consecutive business days. Those distributions are subject to the preferred security’s terms and declarations by the board; a stated annualized rate is not an ironclad future payment guarantee. Common stockholders and preferred investors face different risks and rights. Presenting the preferred yield as though it were a return paid by holding SOL would be inaccurate.

Solana’s price can move substantially faster than a weekly treasury increase, so a company could report more tokens while its dollar portfolio value falls. Staking rewards are also variable and bring their own operational requirements. For DeFi Development, the most informative future disclosures will combine updated token counts with cash reserves, financing costs, issuance, validator income and the amount available to common equity. The accumulation streak is a measurable development, but its investment significance depends on what the company gave up to extend it.

Treasury-company comparisons also require attention to liabilities and timing. Two firms holding similar numbers of SOL can have very different shareholder economics if one borrowed to finance purchases, has preferred dividends to meet or issued substantially more common stock. Reported SOL-per-share figures can be useful, but the numerator and denominator should be consistently defined. Investors should also distinguish income from staking from changes in SOL's market value. Neither measure on its own guarantees liquidity to support future payments or operating expenses.

For related context, see our earlier report on Solana infrastructure updates.

This update is evidence of continued SOL accumulation and preferred-dividend activity. It is not an assurance that either share class will preserve its value, and the reported yield should not be confused with a guaranteed return on the underlying cryptocurrency.

#5102. Marathon Digital Cannot Stop Selling Bitcoin

Bitcoin mining giant MARA Holdings, formerly known as Marathon Digital, continues to offload its Bitcoin holdings, with another multimillion-dollar transfer spotted as the company's selling spree shows no signs of slowing down.

According to blockchain analytics platform Lookonchain, MARA transferred another 366 BTC, worth approximately $23.33 million, from its wallets on Nov. 18.

The latest transaction follows a series of substantial Bitcoin sales by the mining company throughout 2026.

Lookonchain estimates that MARA has already sold a staggering 40,581 BTC this year, generating approximately $3.03 billion at an average selling price of $74,446 per coin.

However, it remains unclear whether the latest 366 BTC transfer represents another completed sale or an internal movement of funds.

MARA's aggressive selling strategy is confirmed by its latest quarterly financial disclosures.

According to its Nov. 9 SEC filing, the company sold approximately 26,984 BTC for $1.9 billion during the first nine months of 2026.

Following the end of September, MARA liquidated another 13,597 BTC at an average price of approximately $81,039, raising an additional $1.1 billion.

These transactions bring its total disclosed Bitcoin sales to 40,581 BTC.

Notably, the company used $750 million from its latest sales to fully repay Bitcoin-backed loans, releasing 17,477 BTC previously pledged as collateral.

Interestingly, MARA has explicitly signaled that it intends to continue selling Bitcoin as part of a broader shift in its corporate strategy.

However, it began allowing sales of newly mined Bitcoin in 2025 before expanding the policy in 2026 to include coins already held on its balance sheet.

In its latest shareholder letter, MARA said it plans to continue monetizing Bitcoin to strengthen its financial flexibility.

The company specifically identified artificial intelligence infrastructure, upcoming convertible debt obligations and potential share repurchases as reasons for building up cash reserves.

The selling comes as MARA faces considerable pressure on its core mining business.

Third-quarter revenue declined 35% year over year to $164.2 million, compared to $252.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

#5100. MEXC Pulls The Plug On VISA Card Months After Launch

Home » Blitz news » MEXC Pulls The Plug On VISA Card Months After Launch

Customers on MEXC’s global exchange can’t use their platform-issued debit cards following an issuer problem.

The exchange announced that its Global Card service ends today, November 18, 2026, at 15:30 UTC after its third-party card issuer made service adjustments. Existing cards will no longer process transactions and new applications are suspended.

The virtual Visa card launched on August 31 with features that included up to 10% USDT cashback and high spending limits. It lasted under three months.

MEXC Global Card Service Update We regret to announce that, following service adjustments by our third-party card issuer, MEXC Global Card services will be discontinued on Nov 18, 2026, at 15:30 UTC. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. We remain… pic.twitter.com/QXLFMeRvd7

The shutdown follows the earlier discontinuation of MEXC’s APAC Card on November 11 over similar issuer issues, and it comes after a temporary maintenance pause that began on November 14.

Cardholders can still withdraw their remaining balances to their MEXC Fiat account before the cutoff.

Any funds left on the card will be snapshotted on November 21 at 15:30 UTC and credited to Spot accounts within three business days.

Refunds for prior transactions will go to Fiat accounts once received, pending cashback continues on schedule, and users are advised to cancel or switch any recurring payments tied to the card.

MEXC has not identified the card issuer or detailed the exact nature of the adjustments. Funds are not frozen; they are being returned to users’ exchange accounts.

#5099. Cypherpunk Reports 8,967 ZEC Mined as Zcash Treasury Nears 342,000 Tokens

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Publicly traded Cypherpunk Technologies has reported the first results from its Zcash mining operation, producing 8,967.29 ZEC in just 44 days. The company says those tokens represented approximately $9.9 million of mining revenue in the third quarter, while its treasury later grew to about 341,859 ZEC through purchases and continued production. The figures are impressive in isolation. But investors need to separate operating earnings from accounting gains on an appreciated token reserve, especially after ZEC’s volatile price action.

Cypherpunk’s November 16 filing says the mining fleet began operation on August 18 and delivered about 95% uptime through September 30. The company reported revenue corresponding to 8,967.29 ZEC, with a stated average cost of mining revenue of approximately $104 per token before depreciation. Once depreciation of equipment is included, the company reported a higher per-token cost near $237. The distinction is crucial when comparing mining economics across companies because machines lose value over time even if their near-term power and hosting costs look low.

Cypherpunk says holdings reached around 341,858.75 ZEC after adding October mining output and recent market purchases, equivalent to roughly 2% of the circulating supply at its reporting date. Its strategy therefore combines an operating mining business with a substantial asset inventory. Both components are sensitive to the cryptocurrency’s price. Tokens generated through mining may be held rather than sold to cover expenses, which can expand exposure and affect cash needs. A higher coin count is not the same as higher spendable cash in the company’s bank accounts.

For related context, see our earlier report on the recent Zcash NU7 protocol upgrade.

The Block reported approximately $2.6 million of quarterly operating profit and substantially greater net income driven by unrealized increases in the value of the ZEC treasury. Valuation gains can be economically relevant, but they can also reverse without an operational change. Investors should read the quarterly income statement and cash-flow statement together. A business with rising book profits may still need external financing to buy new equipment or meet operating expenses if it is retaining mined tokens. The source of earnings determines how repeatable they are.

The company says its fleet represented a material part of Zcash network hashrate at launch, while broader network competition has already changed that percentage. Management has discussed additional equipment purchases for 2027, subject to commitments and delivery. More hardware can produce more hashes, but miner returns depend on network difficulty, rewards, uptime, electricity and ZEC’s price. The most useful follow-up will compare actual production and operating cash with capital spent, rather than treating a treasury-size target as proof of long-term mining profitability.

Mining economics can shift even when a company executes its own operating plan well. As competitors add machines, a given fleet's fraction of network hashrate may fall, reducing expected token output at the same energy cost. Rewards also depend on protocol rules and equipment performance, while treasury purchasing introduces separate exposure to spot prices. Reporting those risks alongside current revenue helps readers understand why one profitable early period does not establish a permanent advantage. A full-year record will offer a stronger measure of the fleet's competitiveness.

For related context, see our earlier report on Bitcoin mining-difficulty changes.

Cypherpunk now has measurable mining output as well as a sizable ZEC balance. The challenge for investors is to value those as two connected but distinct businesses, avoiding the temptation to treat unrealized token appreciation as recurring operational income.

Reporting sources: Cypherpunk Q3 financial results, SEC exhibit · The Block coverage

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has said that crypto needs some of the features that made housing a safe investment for earlier generations. "We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets," Buterin wrote in a post on X on Nov. 18.

The post came a day after economist Peter Tulip published his own post on housing in Raleigh, North Carolina. According to Tulip, looser zoning rules in the city set off a construction boom and pushed real rents down 15% between 2022 and 2025.

In his post, Buterin first pointed to a benefit of young people putting their savings into stocks and crypto instead of real estate.

"One benefit of younger generations investing more in stonks and other digital things instead of housing is that it reduces perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive, instead of rejoicing when prices drop as we do for all other life necessities," he wrote.

Still, the Ethereum co-founder said that housing has had one advantage over stocks and crypto. He described it as "a culture and policy-encouraged default of investing in a safe non-crazy thing that you can't easily liquidate."

"Modern platforms encourage the opposite of this, leading to more irresponsible behavior," Buterin added.

Ether was trading at $1,808 on Wednesday.

Buterin has written about housing and urban planning before. He has supported the YIMBY movement for denser development in cities for several years.

In 2022, Buterin argued for a land value tax. According to him, such a tax would lower the upfront cost of buying a home and discourage speculation on vacant lots.

In 2025, the Ethereum co-founder called the housing market a "confusing market of peculiar NFTs." According to Buterin, what is really being sold under the label of square footage is the right to live in a particular city. At the time, he also said that legalizing dense development speeds up the economy and benefits even people who prefer single-family homes.

#5097. Here’s how Ledger’s website was hit by the Optimizely malware attack

On the 16th of November, Ledger’s public website was infected with malware designed to swap crypto addresses and steal card details. Security researcher Scott Helme traced the code to Optimizely, a website testing provider. His team found compromised scripts tied to 178 organizations, including Ledger, the BBC, and Zoom.

In practice, the malware could swap a copied crypto address for one belonging to the attacker. So if a visitor pasted that address and approved the payment, their crypto could go to the attacker instead.

So far, researchers have traced the malware to Ledger’s public website. Whether it also affected Ledger’s hardware wallets or the Ledger Wallet app remains unclear.

Just over a month earlier, though, Ledger had faced a separate attack involving physical devices. In that case, Ledger confirmed that some wallets sold through a reseller contained unauthorized hardware.

At the time, AMBCrypto reported that the October theft had reached $91 million across more than 470 crypto addresses.

Report URI recorded the cleanup of Ledger’s script at 20:41 UTC that day. Early on the 17th of November, Optimizely said,

We’ve fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects.

Report URI traced about $7,040 in crypto to addresses linked to the attack on the 16th of November. When Galaxy Digital’s Alex Thorn looked at where the money came from, he estimated that victims sent about $2,300. He said,

Most of the rest was the attacker’s own money. The attacker appears to have been very sloppy with their onchain hygiene

However, the number of Ledger visitors who lost funds remains unclear.

A similar breach had hit Polymarket a few weeks earlier. In that case, the malicious code could act on behalf of traders who were already signed in.

On the 29th of October, it sold some traders’ positions and moved funds out of their wallets.

Polymarket paused international trading to stop further losses. It later announced $3.9 million in reimbursements, including about $1.2 million for losses during the pause. By the 30th of October, the company said it had fully refunded 689 of the 726 affected wallets.

#5096. Grayscale Says November Crypto Slump Reflects Stablecoin Exits and Tech-Sector Stress

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Grayscale’s latest market note offers a two-part explanation for the sharp decline in crypto prices: money moving out of stablecoins and pressure spilling over from technology equities. Head of research Zach Pandl argues that fundamental adoption trends remain intact, even while Bitcoin and other large assets struggle. That is the assessment of an asset manager with a commercial interest in digital assets, not a settled finding that the sell-off is over. Its value lies in examining the mechanisms rather than repeating the optimistic conclusion as fact.

The November 16 research note points to accelerating withdrawals from stablecoins after the late-October Binance security incident. When investors redeem dollar-backed tokens for bank deposits, the supply of on-chain dollars can contract. That may reduce the liquidity available for trading and collateral, although it does not mean each redeemed dollar was about to buy Bitcoin. Other drivers can change supply, including arbitrage and issuer operations. Grayscale views off-ramping as one contributing factor to the November weakness. Confirming its influence requires tracking issuance, redemptions and market activity across venues.

The firm also identifies pressure in Nvidia and other AI-linked stocks as a possible source of portfolio de-risking. Investors holding growth technology and crypto exposure may sell both when financing conditions worsen or their risk limits tighten. There is a further link through physical infrastructure: some Bitcoin mining firms are developing high-performance computing services for AI operators. Those connections do not make Bitcoin a direct claim on AI company earnings. They suggest overlapping investors and capital requirements through which stress can travel across otherwise different sectors.

For related context, see our earlier report on stablecoin supply contraction.

Grayscale notes that Bitcoin fell below its 200-day moving average on November 12, a level followed by some trend-oriented trading strategies. Leveraged positions and thinner weekend order books can make subsequent price moves more abrupt. Those mechanisms may amplify a decline without identifying a single fundamental cause. Importantly, technical signals are not universal commands: different funds use different models and time horizons, and a moving-average breach does not determine the market’s next direction. The research describes a chain of plausible forces, not a proven one-factor explanation.

Grayscale believes medium- and long-term investors may find current valuations attractive because institutional stablecoin and tokenization activity continues to develop. The note also acknowledges inflation, interest-rate uncertainty and geopolitical risk. Those headwinds could persist longer than optimistic scenarios assume. Readers should distinguish the factual observation of a significant drawdown from the manager’s valuation judgment. ETF flows, stablecoin supplies and changes in rates can help test the thesis, but none offers a reliable standalone timing signal.

Another test of the explanation is whether on-chain capital actually returns when equity-market stress eases. A rebound in technology shares accompanied by ongoing stablecoin redemptions would suggest the factors are not moving in lockstep. In contrast, renewed stablecoin issuance without a broader Bitcoin recovery would show that liquidity availability alone is insufficient. Such cross-checks are more informative than assigning every daily price move to the same narrative. They also allow readers to separate Grayscale's interpretation from the specific market data used to support it.

For related context, see our earlier report on recent bitcoin ETF outflows.

The report provides a framework for thinking about November’s crypto decline, not proof that prices have bottomed. Its strongest contribution is highlighting how stablecoin redemptions, shared growth-stock positioning and leveraged market structure can interact during a difficult month.

Reporting sources: Grayscale November 16 research note

MEXC confirmed that its Global Card service will be discontinued on November 18, according to the exchange's announcement. The company cites service adjustments by its third-party card issuer. From the deadline, existing cards can no longer be used for transactions, and new card applications are suspended.

Users have two things to take care of before the service ends.

First, the remaining card balance has to be withdrawn: the Withdraw button on the Global Card page sends the funds to the Fiat account.

Second, subscriptions linked to the card should be cancelled or switched to another payment method. Unfortunately for cardholders, recurring payments will most likely fail if they stay on the old card.

If there's still a balance when the service ends, MEXC will credit it to the Spot account, so users will simply receive their funds back. It's important to keep in mind that pending card transactions need time to settle, which is why the balance snapshot comes on November 21, three days after the shutdown. The amount will be credited within three business days of the snapshot. Users do not need to take any action.

Refunds for previous card transactions will be credited to the Fiat account once MEXC receives them. Pending cashback will be credited automatically as scheduled. Elite VVIP users with zero-fee benefits will be refunded too, though the eligible fees return to their Spot accounts only before December 15.

Transaction history, card orders and cashback records stay available on the Global Card page for three months after the service ends, so it's worth saving anything needed before access ends.

Cryptocurrency services delegate certain types of services to third parties all the time, so witnessing a similar situation is more than a possibility here. Realistically, the shutdown is somewhat inconvenient rather than dangerous, as the balances are returned automatically. For users: stay vigilant and try not to put all your eggs in one basket.

Cardano-based stablecoin DJED has announced its sunset, as DJED and SHEN services will wind down on December 31, 2026, at 11:59 pm UTC.

DJED represents a crypto-backed, overcollateralized stablecoin protocol on Cardano whose US-dollar peg is maintained algorithmically against an ADA reserve (with SHEN as the reserve coin), rather than by fiat reserves.

"DJED and SHEN services will wind down at the end of December 31, 2026, at 11:59 pm UTC," a DJED-focused X account wrote.

ATTN: DJED & SHEN Holders DJED and SHEN services will wind down at the end of December 31, 2026 at 11:59pm UTC. Please redeem and convert any DJED and SHEN you hold before then. All redemptions are subject to the reserve ratio.

Users are urged to redeem and convert any DJED and SHEN they hold before this deadline. Users are to redeem on the protocol and convert their DJED and SHEN back to ADA on the official Djed page. Users who hold DJED or SHEN in liquidity pools, lending markets, or other DeFi platforms are urged to withdraw those positions first, then redeem or swap.

The Djed team said all systems are fully operational and redemptions are now open, subject to the reserve ratio. It further added that the Djed protocol will be maintained and remain available until December 31, 2026. After this date, all remaining funds will be allocated to the outstanding DJED/SHEN holders once the wind-down is complete.

Djed’s shutdown comes almost three years after its launch, which came in 2023. The stablecoin was officially launched on the Cardano mainnet on January 31, 2023, and was developed by COTI in collaboration with the Cardano ecosystem to be used on DeFi protocols on Cardano as a stable alternative to volatile cryptocurrencies.

In positive news for the Cardano ecosystem, Monument Bank Limited has launched tokenized deposits on the Midnight network, marking a milestone for the network and the decentralized finance ecosystem.

At present, Monument is the first UK bank to tokenize retail deposits on a public blockchain, offering clients a 5.2% AER fixed-term return on savings directly through its existing banking app, delivering institutional onchain finance through a familiar and user-friendly banking experience.

Up to £250 million of client deposits will be represented on Midnight in this opening phase, with deposits recorded one-to-one in sterling.

#5091. Binance Hack-Linked Wallet Moves 34,279 ETH, but Investigators See No Confirmed Sale

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

A wallet linked by blockchain investigators to the October 29 Binance breach has transferred 34,279.66 ETH to three newly created addresses, ending a period of inactivity. The ether was worth roughly $63 million at prices used in Tuesday’s reporting. That is a significant movement of suspected stolen funds, but a wallet transfer is not automatically a sale, a successful laundering step or proof that the recipient controls are independent of the sender. Investigators had not identified the new addresses as exchanges at the time of their initial reports.

Monitoring groups MistTrack and Solid Intel reported the transfers on November 17. MistTrack described three movements of approximately 12,000 ETH, 12,000 ETH and 10,279.66 ETH. The receiving wallets were newly created, and the monitored funds had not moved again when the analysts published their findings. Public transaction records make it possible to trace the amounts and destinations, but they do not disclose the human operator behind each address. The link to the earlier breach rests on investigators’ attribution of the sending wallet, not a label embedded in the blockchain itself.

The October attack involved vastly larger losses than Tuesday’s movement. US investigators attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking group, and authorities have announced substantial asset restraints and seizures. Blockchain intelligence firms have also tracked funds moved through different assets and protocols. These parallel developments should not be added together casually, because frozen, seized, recovered and still-controlled amounts describe different legal and operational states. The fresh ETH transfers are one piece of a complex post-incident trail rather than an update to the full net-loss number.

For related context, see our earlier report on Coinbase's custody and security precautions.

Crypto trading commentary sometimes treats any transfer from an exploit-linked wallet as preparation to dump tokens. That can happen, but the evidence here does not yet establish a market sale. Transfers may consolidate funds, redistribute control or precede another operation. Until an address is linked to a trading venue, bridge, mixer or other service, the immediate observable fact is the destination change. Even a later exchange deposit would need careful interpretation: deposits are not identical to executed sell orders. Reporting should preserve those steps rather than collapsing them into one dramatic conclusion.

Ethereum’s public ledger lets investigators monitor known addresses and alert service providers if assets reappear at identifiable points. Token issuers, exchanges and law enforcement may each have different powers depending on the assets and jurisdictions involved. Native ETH cannot simply be frozen by an issuer in the way some centrally administered tokens can. That difference complicates recovery when funds leave services that can intervene. The next useful evidence will be further movements, identification of services receiving the funds and official updates to the case.

Investigators can improve attribution confidence by comparing the sequence, amounts and transaction timing with addresses already associated with the incident. Yet public labels can be incomplete, and a newly created wallet may simply be another address controlled by the same actor. Readers should resist claims that funds have reached a criminal group, a particular country or a cash-out desk unless that identification is supported by additional evidence. Future investigative notices should specify their degree of confidence and distinguish observed transfers from hypotheses about their purpose.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Unocoin wallet compromise.

The latest transfer warrants close monitoring, but it should not be reported as the disposal of $63 million in stolen ether without further proof. The distinction between observable transactions and inferred intent is especially important in a security incident of this scale.

Reporting sources: CoinDesk report of MistTrack and Solid Intel monitoring · MistTrack transfer report

#5088. Hackers Redirected Bitcoin Miner Rewards via AI Attack, Luxor CEO Says

Hackers Redirected Bitcoin Miner Rewards via AI Attack, Luxor CEO Says

Hackers briefly hijacked computing power from Bitcoin miners using Luxor’s fleet management software, in what the company’s CEO called an AI-enabled attack.

Luxor Technology said Sunday that its internal monitoring flagged an unauthorized redirect of hashrate through Commander, its tool for managing mining machines.

Hashrate is the computing power miners devote to securing Bitcoin and earning rewards. Just over a dozen client accounts were affected, with their machines pointed to a different mining pool for a limited window, effectively sending the value of their work elsewhere.

Luxor said it patched Commander within two hours and began restoring affected machines to their original settings. No data was leaked or taken from its systems, and the issue was isolated to Commander, according to the company.

Luxor Pool and its LuxOS software weren’t affected, the company said, adding that every affected client will be paid in full for the redirected hashrate, as if their machines had mined normally.

Luxor CEO Nick Hansen said the compromise began around 6 p.m. Pacific time Saturday through “a sophisticated AI-enabled vector.” He didn’t detail how the attack worked. “You trust us with your fleet, and we need to be better,” he wrote on X.

Around 6:00p PDT yesterday, a subset of Commander customers were compromised, through a sophisticated AI-enabled vector. We were able to identify and patch quickly so that it didn't continue, then the hard work of reverting started.…

In a follow-up post, Hansen said crypto businesses are now “inundated with AI-enabled attacks,” with abliterated models, or AI models stripped of their safety guardrails, probing systems around the clock for weaknesses.

Luxor has responded by buying its own bare-metal GPUs to run such models defensively. It has also put most new feature work on hold to harden its infrastructure by rotating keys, updating kernels and pinning dependencies. Hansen urged other companies running similar services to do the same.

Bitcoin developers are grappling with the same threat. Bitcoin Core updated its security policy to address AI-driven threats, and an AI “red team” effort has turned up critical vulnerabilities throughout the year.

The incident also follows other attacks on Bitcoin infrastructure. Blockstream’s Liquid Network restored full Bitcoin backing earlier this month, two months after a $320 million exploit.

Luxor said it would soon publish a full post-mortem of the hack.

#5087. $20 XRP Demand Exposes Ripple’s Legal Boundaries

Home » Trendsetter News » $20 XRP Demand Exposes Ripple’s Legal Boundaries

An open letter urging Ripple to push XRP to $15–$20 has raised concerns about the legal implications of explicit price support.

A demand that Ripple should drive XRP price to $15 – $20 could undermine the legal argument holders spent years defending, wealth focused commentator Kamilah Stevenson warns in her video.

Her concern is that an explicit price-support pledge could strengthen claims that buyers expect profits from Ripple’s efforts.

The open letter, posted anonymously on X on November 1, addresses Ripple executives Brad Garlinghouse and David Schwartz. It accuses the company of prioritizing RLUSD and other businesses over XRP and calls for market action to lift the token’s price.

Dr. Stevenson cites attorney Bill Morgan’s objection: the letter asks Ripple to provide the very support that holders argued they had not relied on when buying XRP. “XRP holders bought a digital asset, not shares of Ripple,” she says, describing pushback against the letter.

That distinction matters under the Howey test, which examines whether an arrangement involves an investment of money in a common enterprise with an expectation of profits derived from others’ efforts.

In July 2023, Judge Analisa Torres distinguished between Ripple’s institutional sales and its programmatic exchange sales.

About $728 million in institutional sales constituted investment contracts; the programmatic sales at issue did not, with the court emphasizing the circumstances of those transactions, including buyers’ lack of knowledge about whom they were paying.

The ruling did not give every future XRP transaction blanket protection. Equally, one holder’s letter does not change XRP’s legal treatment: Dr. Stevenson’s warning concerns what Ripple might promise or do in response.

The YouTube video recalls the trading restrictions that followed the SEC’s December 2020 lawsuit. Coinbase suspended XRP trading in January 2021 and restored it after the July 2023 ruling, leaving U.S. customers without that trading venue for roughly two and a half years.

Dr. Kamilah Stevenson argues that Ripple should instead build reasons to use XRP, pointing to payments and its acceptance as collateral at Ripple Prime. Those activities are different from promising holders a particular XRP price.

#5085. US Senators Question SEC Tokenized-Stock Exemption Over Wallet Transfers and Investor Protection

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Four Democratic US senators have pressed the Securities and Exchange Commission for answers about how its new approach to tokenized stock trading will protect investors and prevent illicit transfers. Their November 16 letter, reported by The Block, takes aim at gaps they see in the SEC’s five-year innovation exemption for certain trading venues. The development is an oversight challenge, not a court ruling or a notice that the exemption has been cancelled. It goes to a central difficulty for tokenized securities: a regulated purchase can become a blockchain transfer to another address.

The SEC introduced its approach in September, allowing qualifying tokenized-securities venues to operate under a defined exemption from some ordinary exchange-registration requirements. The aim is to permit experimentation with trading stocks in token form while the agency assesses a new market structure. A token representing a security still raises questions about ownership, trading rules and investor rights. The exemptions and their precise conditions matter more than a general statement that securities have moved on-chain. Not every blockchain token, broker or venue automatically qualifies for the same regulatory treatment.

Senators Angela Alsobrooks, Ruben Gallego, Mark Warner and Catherine Cortez Masto reportedly told SEC Chair Paul Atkins that the framework lacks sufficiently specific safeguards around know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering procedures. A buyer verified by a regulated venue might later transfer a token to a wallet whose controller has not undergone the same checks. This problem is not solved merely by verifying the identity of the first purchaser. The letter asks how secondary transfers and the reach of compliance obligations would be managed once tokens circulate beyond the initial venue.

For related context, see our earlier report on Hong Kong's developing licensing rules.

The senators raised concerns about retail-investor protections and pricing, and reportedly asked whether companies could opt out of having their shares tokenized. Those questions are distinct from financial-crime screening. A token that references equity needs a clear relationship to the rights and obligations of the underlying security, as well as fair information about execution and ownership. If an issuer’s wishes, the investor’s expectations and the platform’s legal structure do not line up, technical transferability alone cannot resolve the conflict. Policymakers must address those issues in enforceable terms.

The lawmakers asked the SEC to explain its approach and urged a transparent rulemaking process for changes in the regulatory treatment of tokenized securities. Such a letter can affect oversight and public debate, especially as control of congressional committees changes, but it is not itself binding legislation. Venues exploring tokenized equities should continue to follow the actual exemption terms and any subsequent SEC guidance. The next concrete milestones are the agency’s response, proposed revisions if any, and how early trading models implement identity, custody and transfer restrictions.

For related context, see our earlier report on new institutional crypto-custody arrangements.

Tokenization can change how securities move, but it does not automatically settle which rules should accompany them. The dispute now concerns the design of that regulatory perimeter, with no basis to describe the senators’ letter as an immediate prohibition on tokenized stocks.

Reporting sources: The Block report of four senators’ letter

Bitcoin's 200-week moving average (200WMA) has climbed above $68,000 for the first time, Blockstream CEO Adam Back noted on X on Nov. 18. "Bitcoin passes $68k 200wma," he wrote. Back attached a 200-week moving average heatmap from Look Into Bitcoin, and the chart shows the indicator rising throughout Bitcoin's history. On Nov. 18, the indicator was between $67,955 and $68,145.

#bitcoin passes $68k 200wma https://t.co/dgIzS9Nsvw https://t.co/xzYdP0EvZh

Back is the cryptographer behind Hashcash. The algorithm laid the groundwork for proof-of-work, and Satoshi Nakamoto cited it in the Bitcoin white paper. Back was also one of the first people Satoshi contacted before the launch of Bitcoin in 2009.

The Blockstream CEO has posted about the 200WMA on X several times this year. On March 27, he wrote that the "200wma passes $59k." The indicator was just above $60,000 in early May, and on May 30, Back reported that it had crossed $61,000. In September, the 200WMA rose above $65,000 for the first time.

In a follow-up post in May, Back cited a maxim of the late Charlie Munger. According to Munger, an investor who buys only high-quality assets when they trade at the 200-week moving average would beat the S&P 500 over time. Back also noted that Munger and Warren Buffett never embraced Bitcoin.

In mid-September, Bitcoin was trading at around $76,000 to $77,000. At that time, the gap between the price and the 200WMA was more than $10,000.

On Wednesday, Bitcoin was trading at $64,150, about 6% below the 200WMA. On Nov. 15, BTC dropped as low as $62,000 before bouncing 5.5%. Back called the move "bouncy" in a post on X.

In a CNBC interview on Nov. 12, Back said that Bitcoin could reach $1 million by 2028. According to Back, more than 95% of potential institutional inflows into Bitcoin are still ahead. He named investment trusts, asset managers and corporate treasuries among the buyers, and he said that their buying was just beginning.

Back also pointed to the Bitcoin halving in the spring of 2028. He said that miners would sell fewer coins after it.

He made a similar point at Paris Blockchain Week in April. "When the Bitcoin price is low, the miners have to sell a bigger proportion… and when the price is higher, they don't have to sell as much," Back said at the time.

Cloud mining allows users to mine cryptocurrencies by renting computing power. They can mine crypto without buying or owning any equipment or worrying about its maintenance. Mining is an essential part of the cryptocurrency space, and with cloud mining, the space is opened up for people with little to no technical knowledge.

Cloud mining provides an alternative to anyone in the crypto space who wants to participate in Bitcoin mining without buying any expensive mining equipment or managing hardware. Here is our list of the top 7 cloud mining platforms of the month:

NiceHash has a marketplace that provides an alternative to conventional cloud mining contracts instead of functioning as a fixed-term mining provider. Instead of functioning as a fixed-term mining provider, it connects hashrate buyers and sellers through a marketplace.

For users who want to understand mining costs and rewards and monitor prices, it is a great option. The platform also supports proof-of-work algorithms and lets users mine Bitcoin and other PoW assets through pools of their choice, where payouts are settled in BTC.

KuMining is associated with the KuCoin ecosystem and gives users a chance to explore cryptocurrency mining contracts without having their own mining machines. Users can compare various available mining contracts in terms of hashrate pricing, mining durations, and choose the right one depending on their requirements.

Since KuCoin is an established exchange ecosystem, KuMining gained a lot of attention through it. Users who understand exchange-based accounts and digital asset transactions can find the platform to be useful. It is a good option for existing crypto traders who want to use mining services related to an exchange.

ViaBTC is popular and known for its mining pool services and lets users connect their mining equipment to a shared mining pool and take part in cryptocurrency reward distribution. Most of the platform’s services are for users who are already part of mining hardware operations and want to establish a pool rather than attempting to mine on their own.

Multiple cryptocurrencies and mining-related tools on the platform allow users to monitor account balances, payout information, and mining performance. ViaBTC can be great for anyone who wants to research professional mining operations and alternative mining pool services.

Hashing24 is for users who want to focus on accessing mining capacity through contract-based arrangements. For anyone wanting to be a part of cloud mining without buying ASIC hardware or managing it.

It has been a part of the cryptocurrency space since 2012 and focuses primarily on Bitcoin mining. Users can buy mining power that is measured in terahashes, with contracts running over different periods of time depending on the plan.

BeMine has fractional ownership of ASIC mining hardware rather than relying on renting traditional cloud mining contracts. The mining company is based on the principles of security and transparency. Mining can be done without the owner’s direct participation.

Users can also buy 1/100 of a share of any specific ASIC, which can be a viable option for anyone who wants to start mining without buying an expensive machine entirely.

BitFuFu is another popular option for users, and it operates in the Bitcoin mining infrastructure sector and offers options for miner sales, mining equipment hosting, and cloud mining. The platform aims to empower the global Bitcoin network and offers a one-stop solution for a cheap and easy way to earn Bitcoin.

There is an online interface that lets users monitor mining-related information and account activity, making it easy and convenient for those who are new to the space.

Bitdeer provides cloud hashrate services, infrastructure services, and mining hardware solutions for a wide range of users. The cloud mining products let users buy computing power without buying or maintaining any mining machines. They can also choose the hashrate capacities and mining durations that suit their requirements well.

The company is also involved in large-scale mining infrastructure and operates mining facilities and provides services connected to cryptocurrency mining hardware.

Cloud mining is an alternative and interesting way for users to become a part of the cryptocurrency space. While the crypto mining space may look daunting for a lot of people, cloud mining provides an easy segue into it.

Every platform mentioned on this list has its own advantages; however, it is advised to do your own research before investing.

Geneva, Switzerland –  TRON DAO, the community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet through blockchain technology and decentralized applications (dApps), today announced that the Aave App, a high-yield savings mobile app developed and managed by Aave Labs, will add support for USDT (TRC-20) deposits on the TRON network as it expands to Android following its initial launch on iOS.

The launch combines Android’s global reach with TRON’s leading role in the stablecoin ecosystem, expanding mobile access to onchain savings opportunities that are not accessible on traditional savings apps. With support for USDT on TRON, eligible users in supported jurisdictions can now deposit USDT on TRON and start earning yield on their savings.

Android’s extensive global footprint offers a significant distribution opportunity for digital asset applications, particularly in markets where stablecoins are used for payments, remittances, and savings. TRON provides an established infrastructure for this opportunity, with more than $94 billion in circulating USDT, the largest circulating supply of Tether’s dollar-pegged stablecoin among blockchain networks. TRON also supports a broad range of stablecoin use cases, including payments, cross-border transfers, and digital asset transactions.

Aave is building the World’s Savings App, a simple, globally accessible tool designed to help people grow and manage their savings, with a delightful design experience on the surface and powerful onchain finance infrastructure working under the hood. Users of the app can earn yield on their savings, enjoy flexible access to their funds, and benefit from the Balance Protection program. They can also deposit and withdraw via stablecoins or banks in eligible countries and project their potential savings growth over the years with a future simulator. Following its availability on iOS, the Android launch expands the app’s mobile reach, while TRON support connects users to one of the largest USDT ecosystems in onchain finance.

“Aave Labs has a proven track record of building leading DeFi products, and the Aave App brings that expertise to everyday users,” said Justin Sun, Founder of TRON. “With TRON support on Android and iOS, more people can use the USDT they already hold on TRON to access simple, accessible onchain savings with the Aave App.”

“Millions of people in emerging economies already rely on stablecoins on TRON to save and send money,” said Stani Kulechov, Founder and CEO of Aave Labs. “The Aave App lets them earn on those dollars.”

By enabling USDT deposits through the Aave App on Android, the integration connects TRON’s established stablecoin ecosystem with a consumer-focused mobile application. The launch reflects the continued convergence of mobile applications and blockchain infrastructure, as consumer-focused products work to make digital assets and decentralized financial services more accessible worldwide.

TRON DAO is a community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet via blockchain technology and dApps.

Founded in September 2017, the TRON blockchain has experienced significant growth since its MainNet launch in May 2018. Today, TRON hosts the largest circulating supply of USD Tether (USDT) stablecoin, which currently exceeds $94 billion. As of November 2026, the TRON blockchain has recorded over 414 million in total user accounts, more than 16 billion in total transactions, and over $24 billion in total value locked (TVL), based on TRONSCAN. #5081. XRP Treasury Takes $505 Million Accounting Hit

Home » Ripple (XRP) » XRP Treasury Takes $505 Million Accounting Hit

Evernorth, the openly-traded XRP-only corporate treasury, took in a big loss despite not selling one coin.

Evernorth Holdings has marked down the value of its pre-listing XRP holdings by roughly 60%, booking about $505 million in cumulative impairment charges despite not selling the tokens.

The company’s latest quarterly filing showed 346 million XRP carried at approximately $341.9 million as of Sept. 30, down from an original recorded cost basis near $847 million.

The write-down reflects accounting treatment rather than a realized sale or reduction in the size of the treasury.

Under the accounting rules applied in the filing, XRP is treated as an indefinite-lived intangible asset. That requires a company to reduce the carrying value when the token’s market price falls below its purchase cost.

🚨UPDATE: Evernorth Is DOWN Over $505 MILLION On Its 346 MILLION $XRP Holdings WITHOUT Selling Them 🤯🔥Okay, I was looking into Evernorth’s November 13 @SECGov filing, and the numbers are INSANE! 👀👉 Its $XRP treasury has lost roughly 60% of its original recorded value,… https://t.co/U1rVkPSMpA pic.twitter.com/OvgxV7d75U

Those impairment charges cannot simply be reversed if XRP later recovers, meaning the balance-sheet value may remain below the market value of the holdings unless the assets are sold.

The accounting treatment can therefore leave a lasting gap between a company’s reported digital-asset value and the price investors see in the market.

The filing put Evernorth’s total assets at about $348.9 million, almost entirely represented by digital assets. It also listed total liabilities of roughly $534.5 million and an accumulated deficit of about $185.6 million.

The 346 million XRP figure covers Evernorth’s pre-merger balance sheet at the end of September.

Following the completion of its merger in October, the combined business was reported to hold about 473 million XRP, with additional tokens previously held through a separate affiliated entity.

SEC FILING: Evernorth files a prospectus supplement to register the resale of up to 73.7M Class A shares and 239,653 sponsor warrants.The company will not receive proceeds from the resale, except on exercise of the sponsor warrants.Last reported price (Nov 16): $7.45 per… https://t.co/wXcQPJQwS5 pic.twitter.com/FakZLekF9s

That makes the filing an important snapshot rather than a complete measure of the company’s current XRP exposure.

It also underscores the concentrated nature of Evernorth’s strategy: its asset base and future operating plans remain closely tied to one highly fluctuating cryptocurrency.

Evernorth has outlined plans to seek returns from its XRP reserves through liquidity provision, lending and options-related activity on the XRP Ledger.

Those initiatives could eventually create revenue, but the filing showed no revenue through the period covered.

#5079. Bitcoin's $2 Billion Liquidation Weekend Leaves Traders Watching $60,000

Bitcoin's $2 Billion Liquidation Weekend Leaves Traders Watching $60,000

Bitcoin fell to around $62,100 on Sunday as roughly $2 billion in crypto derivatives positions were forcibly closed, mostly bets that prices would rise. The weekend slide sent the cryptocurrency to its lowest level since July 14, adding another ugly chapter to six consecutive weeks of losses.

Bitcoin had recovered to around $64,300 early Monday. But the options market is showing why traders aren't necessarily treating that bounce as an all-clear.

Liquidations happen when an exchange closes a trader's position because the money posted to support a borrowed bet is no longer enough to cover its losses. CoinGlass figures from Saturday showed $1.9 billion liquidated in one 24-hour period, about $1.8 billion of it bullish positions across cryptocurrencies, not just Bitcoin.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs had already been losing investors before the weekend. Data from Decrypt’s ETF tracker show $185.4 million in net outflows on Friday, extending their losing streak to seven trading sessions and bringing withdrawals since November 5 to approximately $1.91 billion.

BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $143.5 million of Friday's withdrawals, while Fidelity's FBTC lost $41.9 million. The funds' earlier weakness had helped explain the broader exodus, although ETF flow totals measure fund creations and redemptions rather than every trade between investors.

Those numbers also come with a timing distinction: U.S. ETFs do not trade over the weekend, while Bitcoin trades around the clock. Friday's outflows show weakened demand before the crash, not that ETF shareholders were redeeming shares during Sunday's plunge.

Bitcoin's technical indicators suggest the selling may be overstretched, but that doesn't necessarily mean the worst is over.

The daily Relative Strength Index sat near 24 in oversold territory on the daily charts. Meanwhile, the Average Directional Index stood above 33, indicating a strong prevailing trend, with bearish directional pressure still dominating. The weekly RSI, near 38, pointed to a weak longer-term picture, although it had not reached oversold territory.

The cryptocurrency bounced after approaching support around $62,000. A recovery would face potential resistance near $66,500 to $67,200, followed by another obstacle around $69,300, based on the chart's Fibonacci levels that measure support and resistance marks.

A decisive break below $62,000, meanwhile, would put the psychologically important $60,000 level back in focus—precisely where options traders have accumulated significant downside exposure.

Bitcoin's next test will be whether fresh U.S. ETF flow data show more withdrawals for Monday and whether traders keep paying for downside protection. The heavily watched November 27 options expiration is still ahead, with $50,000 puts among the contracts drawing the most recent trading activity.

The Solana Foundation now holds a “majority interest” in CoinGecko, its Chief Product Officer Vibhu Norby said on X.

CoinGecko described the arrangement as “backing” when it announced the news at Breakpoint in London on the 17th of November. Neither announcement gave the exact stake, price, or governance terms.

Four days earlier, CoinGecko had promoted independent ownership as a reason to choose its data service over Binance-owned CoinMarketCap. It now plans to explore trading alongside its market data.

The Foundation said it planned to bring Solana-powered trading to CoinGecko’s website, app, and GeckoTerminal. Notably, CoinGecko said it was still exploring trading features.

For Solana, that could mean reaching traders where they already look up prices. CoinGecko draws well over 50 million monthly sessions, according to the Foundation.

Norby also flagged broader coverage of stocks and real-world assets [RWAs]. AMBCrypto reported that Solana’s RWA value reached $5 billion in October.

CoinGecko’s API guide warned that exchange ownership could raise questions about bias in rankings and trading volumes. AMBCrypto covered similar concerns when Binance bought CoinMarketCap in 2020.

After Norby’s disclosure, an X user called the new arrangement “a credibility problem.”

CoinGecko said its methods would stay “transparent, publicly accessible.” Readers can check how it calculates prices, but the announcements leave open who can approve changes to those rules.

Brera Holdings disclosed board rights in a separate 2025 deal involving Solmate. A later filing specified that the Foundation could nominate up to two directors, depending on board size. For CoinGecko, board seats and approval rights remain undisclosed.

#5075. XRP’s Native Chain First To Clear CertiK’s GL1 Verification

Home » Ripple (XRP) » XRP’s Native Chain First To Clear CertiK’s GL1 Verification

XRP Ledger’s node operators’ self-attestations were assessed using a new gold standard in blockchain security.

CertiK has completed independent technical verification of self-attestations submitted by the XRP Ledger Foundation and Partior under the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit.

The toolkit supplies a common set of controls for assessing digital financial infrastructures. It draws on international standards and industry practices and was developed under the GL1 initiative involving financial institutions and policymakers.

The next phase is now being advanced by the Global Layer One Organisation, a Singapore-based non-profit founded by HSBC, Kinexys by J.P. Morgan, MUFG Bank, Societe Generale-FORGE, and Standard Chartered.

CertiK reviewed all 112 controls in the toolkit to determine which ones could be checked through independent technical methods. It then examined the network operators’ self-attestations against supporting evidence that included code, configurations, logs, and test results.

🔥 BIG! #XRPL becomes the first public, permissionless Layer 1 blockchain to have its GL1 Architecture and Resiliency principles independently verified by CertiK, signaling its readiness for institutional-grade market infrastructure 👏🏻 $XRP https://t.co/FzvcoAMaP0 pic.twitter.com/oXUo8ieQL8

The work focused on the Architecture and Resiliency principles.

As tokenized-asset activity increases, clearer visibility into how infrastructure controls are actually implemented can help institutions evaluate operational and risk-management fit. Independent verification adds a layer of evidence beyond the operators’ own statements.

“Institutions developing and expanding tokenized asset services need to understand how the controls supporting their infrastructure have been implemented,” said Esme Pau, CertiK’s Head of Capital Markets and Policy.

“Independent technical verification helps operators substantiate their self-attestations and gives institutions evidence they can weigh in their own infrastructure assessments.”

#5073. Countdown to Upgrade: Only 4 Votes Needed for XRP Ledger Vault to Go Live in 2026

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. The Single Asset Vault amendment on the XRP Ledger is getting closer to activation on the mainnet as validator support builds for the network’s preparation to enable better DeFi functionality.

According to data from XRPScan, the SingleAssetVault amendment, or XLS-65, has received yes votes from 25 of 35 trusted validators, currently standing at 71.43% consensus as of November 18, 2026. It needs more than 80% of 35 votes (29) to start its 14-day countdown to activation. That means it needs four more votes to get there and could reach the magic number before the end of 2026.

The XRP Ledger’s amendment process requires a proposed amendment to be approved by more than 80% of trusted validators for 14 days before it is implemented. Validator support may shift during this time, and if the required 80% threshold is lost, activation may be delayed.

The Single Asset Vault amendment creates a structure for aggregating assets from multiple depositors and is intended to be used with the on-chain Lending Protocol. The amendment introduces a Vault object that defines the state of a tokenized vault, and the Vault entry is one of the ledger entry types it provides.

The Vault object holds important information such as available assets, shares, total value, and other relevant information. Users can create a Vault object with the VaultCreate transaction; the Vault object is tracked in an Owner Directory owned by the Vault Owner account.

The XRP Ledger lending amendment has gained additional yes votes. According to XRPScan, the LendingProtocolV1_1 amendment, also known as XLS-66, has received 24 yes votes out of 35 trusted validators, meaning it has 68.57% consensus as of November 18, 2026. It needs more than 80% of the 35 votes (29) to trigger a 14-day activation countdown.

This implies that there are five votes left for it to reach this threshold, with the possibility of it securing the required number of votes before the end of 2026 as well.

According to XRP enthusiasts, LendingProtocolV1_1 represents the biggest amendment for unlocking capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger and is anticipated by institutional and retail users.

#5072. Bitcoin Wallet Maker Trezor Says Customer Data Was Exposed Again

Bitcoin Wallet Maker Trezor Says Customer Data Was Exposed Again

The “days since last third-party breach” counter at Trezor has reset to zero once again.

This time, hackers accessed shipping partner Skladon's systems and likely exported information tied to approximately 27,000 hardware-wallet orders, according to a company disclosure published Monday.

The intrusion occurred November 7, but Skladon did not notify Trezor until November 15. The exposed records cover orders placed between August 9 and November 7, including customers' full names, phone numbers, delivery and email addresses, plus the products they bought and their prices.

Trezor said its own systems were not compromised, and no wallet backups, PINs or passphrases were involved. The breach does not, by itself, let an attacker move a buyer's coins, but it gives them a potentially dangerous combination: a home address and evidence that someone bought a device designed to store crypto.

The latest incident follows an August shipping partner hack and a September email provider breach, making three separate third-party security incidents in a little over three months.

Trezor said some customers have already reported fraudulent phone calls. Criminals could cite the exact model and price of a wallet to make an unsolicited call, text or letter seem legitimate, or use a home address to identify someone who may hold cryptocurrency.

In August, logistics provider ShipMonk suffered a breach that initially appeared to affect fewer than 14,000 Trezor customers. An updated investigation uncovered records for another 67,000 U.S. buyers from 2019 to 2021 that ShipMonk had retained despite assurances they had been deleted, bringing the total to 80,689 people.

September brought another incident, this time at marketing email provider Brevo. Hackers used Trezor's legitimate email channel to distribute a fake security warning urging recipients to install an app that requested their wallet backups. Trezor later said 347,149 email addresses had been exported.

These weren't Trezor's first brushes with the problem. A Mailchimp insider attack targeted Trezor users in 2022, and a 2024 breach of its external support portal put the contact details of up to 66,000 people at risk.

The fallout can go beyond inbox spam. In February, fake letters were sent to hardware-wallet owners, complete with Trezor branding, holograms and QR codes leading to phishing sites.

Asked why an order from Trezor's official store involved an outside company, Trezor responded that it’s basically a logistics question, not a tech issue. “Companies of our size and global reach can’t run efficiently without third-party service providers,” the company replied to a comment on X.

Hi, companies of our size and global reach can’t run efficiently without third-party service providers. Handling as much as possible internally is the goal, but doing every part of the business ourselves isn’t realistic. Skladon is one of the partners that delivers Trezor orders,…

It said Skladon held only the information needed to deliver parcels, and handling every stage of global distribution in-house was not realistic.

Trezor says Skladon does not ship to the United States, so American buyers were not affected by this incident. Affected customers have been notified where possible, though some people who ordered between August 9 and 14 may not receive an email because Trezor had already anonymized their records.

The company has introduced anonymous pickup at parcel lockers or collection points in 18 European countries, allowing buyers to avoid supplying a home address. It is also working to shorten retention of order data from 90 to 45 days and says shipping partners will have to follow the same policy.

Trezor advises customers to ignore unexpected calls and messages about their orders, check any concerns through its official support site and never share a wallet backup. It has notified a data protection authority, but has not yet disclosed how attackers got into Skladon's systems.

#5070. America’s $1 trillion AI data center boom just suffered its first slowdown in over a year

US data center construction plunged 28% in the third quarter, but an October rebound suggests the infrastructure boom could still set another record.

US data center construction fell 28% in the third quarter of 2026, marking its first quarterly decline in more than a year as questions mount over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom.

According to data released by Cleanview, developers began construction on facilities representing 8.4 gigawatts of power capacity between July and September, down from a record 11.7 GW in the preceding quarter.

The number of buildings starting construction also fell to 65 from 96, although the quarter still ranked third-highest in Cleanview's records and was up 55% from the same period last year.

US buildings that began vertical construction in October 2026.

Three buildings accounted for about 35% of the second-highest month in Cleanview’s series.

Cleanview rounds the monthly total. It dates each start to the beginning of vertical construction.

Add the three reported October building contributions (720 + 461 + 450 = 1,631 MW) and divide by 4,600 MW. The resulting share, 35.46%, is shown as about 35% because the monthly total is rounded. The rows use a common scale to compare the building values.

Cleanview rounds the monthly total. It dates each start to the beginning of vertical construction.

The slowdown raises questions about an industry whose expansion has become central to the global AI investment boom.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Michael Thomas, founder of Cleanview Energy, estimated that data centers whose construction began this year will cost approximately $1 trillion to build and equip. He said:

“A lasting slowdown would reach the utilities planning new power plants, the companies making chips and turbines, and a stock market that has bet heavily on AI.”

The findings are based on Cleanview's analysis of thousands of satellite images tracking construction activity at more than 1,300 data center buildings across the United States.

Despite the third-quarter slowdown, construction activity rebounded sharply in October, with developers starting facilities representing 4.6 GW of capacity.

That was the second-highest monthly total Cleanview has recorded and nearly double the capacity that began construction in October 2025.

Three major projects accounted for approximately 35% of the month's activity. These included 720 megawatts at Nscale's Monarch campus in West Virginia, 461 MW at Related Digital's Stargate Michigan campus and 450 MW at Crusoe's Abilene campus in Texas.

Together, the projects represented approximately 1.63 GW of new construction starts, highlighting the scale of investment still flowing into AI infrastructure.

In view of this, Thomas said it was too early to conclude that the third-quarter decline signaled a lasting slowdown.

This is because October's strong rebound could push fourth-quarter construction starts to a record 14 GW if the pace continues through November and December.

Memecoins often produce sharp short-term moves that can fade quickly when broader risk appetite remains uncertain. PEPE’s latest recovery may indicate that some buyers are stepping in near lower levels, but it remains too early to treat that activity as evidence of sustained demand.

A firm hold above $0.00000383 would give bulls a stronger foundation for extending the rebound. A loss of that level, however, could expose the token to renewed selling pressure and reinforce concerns that the latest move was only a temporary pause in a broader market dip.

Price action in highly speculative tokens can turn rapidly, particularly when trading is driven by short-term positioning rather than fresh fundamental developments. PEPE coin remains especially sensitive to shifts in market mood, with traders likely to watch whether buying volume follows the price recovery.

The immediate setup is therefore straightforward: consolidation above support would suggest that sellers are losing some control, while another rejection could leave the token vulnerable to further downside. Neither PEPE’s price outcome is guaranteed: volatility remains the central risk.

#5067. Alibaba's Qwen 4 Max Leads China's AI Agent Race—But You Can't Download It

Alibaba's Qwen 4 Max Leads China's AI Agent Race—But You Can't Download It

Alibaba released Qwen 4 Max on Monday, its most powerful AI model yet and the first flagship built on its new Qwen 4 architecture.

It is also the highest-ranked Chinese model on Arena's agent leaderboard, putting the company ahead of Tencent, Moonshot AI and DeepSeek in that particular test.

The new model has 2.4 trillion parameters, can process text, images and video, and accepts up to one million tokens of context. Parameters are all the different dials a model can handle and tweak when processing information. Tokens are basically the smallest unit of information a model can handle. Its current configuration is enough room for lengthy codebases or stacks of documents.

Alibaba uses a mixture-of-experts design, which keeps most of those parameters idle for any given word it processes. Qwen 4 Max activates 71 billion at a time, compared with 95 billion for Qwen 3.8 Max, allowing a very large model to use less computing power per token.

On Agent Arena, Qwen 4 Max placed 14th among individual models and made Alibaba the fifth-ranked laboratory overall.

The leaderboard evaluates real agent sessions using task completion, user satisfaction and how well models respond to corrections, then scores each model by its net percentage improvement over an average competitor. Qwen 4 Max posted a preliminary 7.46% score across 14,727 sessions, the highest among Chinese entries.

Its visual work may be the more interesting part for regular users. The Code Arena web-development ranking compares websites built by AI models using head-to-head user votes and a points-based rating system. Qwen 4 Max debuted sixth globally at 1,750 points, up 74 from its predecessor, and placed eighth in categories for branding and reference-based design.

That puts it in the same neighborhood as the best American models at turning a request, a screenshot or a rough idea into a working interface that actually looks good.

Alibaba's demos go further, showing the model building game environments and translating factory layouts into 3D models, although those are company-selected examples rather than independent tests.

The visual capability is for understanding images and video and producing code or other text-based outputs. It is not the same as releasing a new image generator.

Qwen 4 Max costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million generated tokens through QwenCloud, a 25% reduction from the previous flagship's $2 and $6 rates. Reused input served from an automatic cache costs $0.075 per million tokens, which can make repetitive workflows substantially cheaper.

Alibaba says its internal testing across hundreds of professional specialties found that the model used 35% fewer tokens and reduced average task costs by roughly 60% compared with Qwen 3.8 Max. In other words, it should be cheaper to execute tasks on this model even against competitors with a similar price..

The bigger limitation for the community is that Qwen 4 Max is closed-weight. Developers can use it through an API or Alibaba's apps, but they cannot download its internal parameters, modify it or run it privately on their own hardware.

Qwen has become a foundation for the open-model ecosystem. An August report from Hugging Face counted 151,448 Qwen-based derivative models on its platform, about 4.7 times the number built specifically on Meta's Llama family. Those include community fine-tunes and optimized versions that power local assistants and specialized tools.

Alibaba opened the weights of Qwen 3.8 Max earlier this year, despite having kept some previous Max models proprietary. It also previewed elements of the Qwen 4 architecture with smaller models months before Monday's release.

The launch lands in a crowded Chinese race. Moonshot's Kimi K3 pushed enormous open-weight models toward Western performance, while DeepSeek has been competing hard on API prices.

Qwen 4 Max leads some Chinese rankings, but American labs still hold the top spots in Arena's overall agent and web-development tables. They are also considerably more expensive.

Alibaba says smaller Qwen 4 models will be released with open weights, giving developers a chance to build on this generation rather than simply rent its biggest model. It has not announced their sizes or release dates.
